authority.staged_bundle_hashes_omitted_reason: a .skill zip's sha256 is not a content identity: zip headers carry per-file mtimes and cowork_workspace_install.sh re-runs the packager on every install, so the same content hashes differently (measured: 3a4923e17aa626d4 vs f80581dcfacd36dd). skill_md_git_blob and content_sha256 below are the content anchors; s07's drift check must use those, not a zip sha.
authority.content_anchor_recipe: Both per-bundle anchors below are defined by tests/test_cowork_skill_verbs.py::derive_bundles, which is their normative definition; s07 must reproduce these values, not invent its own. content_sha256: take every file under the bundle directory (Path.rglob('*'), is_file(), NO suffix filter -- the packager filters nothing either), sorted by absolute path (equivalently by relative path -- every file shares the bundle prefix); feed one sha256 in that order with, per file, the file's path RELATIVE to the bundle dir as POSIX text, then a single NUL byte (b'\0'), then the file's raw bytes; the hex digest is the bundle's content_sha256. No zip, no mtime, no subprocess, so it is stable across re-packaging. skill_md_git_blob: the git blob sha1 of SKILL.md's raw bytes, i.e. sha1(b'blob <len>\0' + data), computed in-process (helper _git_blob_sha1).

recorded_not_changed: egress.withheld is an ENGINE-WIDE, caller-influenced counter carried by EVERY content verb EXCEPT grep and graph-expand, which drop above-ceiling notes PRE-MATCH. So the surviving existence channel is not confined to the ranked legs (search/hybrid_search/diagnose, where it is query-dependent, including inside diagnose's 'withheld' refusal). It is sharpest on the EXACT-TARGET verbs, where the caller names the thing it is probing: get/read and bases-query. Re-measured 2026-08-28 through mcp_adapter.dispatch at max_tier=Internal on a two-note fixture -- read/get id=mnpi-secret -> {result: null, egress: {total: 1, surfaced: 0, withheld: 1}}; id=no-such-note-xyz -> {result: null, egress: {total: 0, surfaced: 0, withheld: 0}}; bases-query where classification=MNPI -> withheld 1, a predicate matching nothing -> withheld 0. A caller can therefore confirm a note's existence by guessing its id, or the presence of any frontmatter predicate, without receiving a document. TRIGGER, and it is narrow: this crosses a boundary only where the OPERATOR has narrowed $BRAIN_MAX_EGRESS_TIER below the vault's top tier. Under the shipped host default (full vault, owner ruling 2026-08-17) a capped max_tier is self-imposed by the caller and nothing is being withheld from anyone. NOT changed, on get/read and bases-query as well as on the ranked legs: the counter is the engine-wide elevation contract (egress.hint, AGENTS.md 'a starved result means elevate, not give up') and it is shared with the CLI twins, where `brain get --json` DELIBERATELY distinguishes {error: not_found} exit 1 from {error: withheld_by_egress_filter} exit 2 -- there the oracle IS the elevation signal, stated out loud (both re-measured 2026-08-28). Pre-dropping inside the MCP verb alone would fork the broker's get from its --json twin, which is the CLI-shape parity DESK-02 exists to keep; pre-dropping at the root would delete that documented CLI distinction for every capped read. Either is an engine-wide egress decision, not one to settle inside one verb. That is the difference from graph-expand, which WAS closed: its fix went in at the root (brain.graph.graph_expand gained max_tier=), so the CLI twin moved with it and parity held. For S06's whole-surface pass, which must sweep every content verb rather than confirm this list. STILL OPEN, still recorded-not-changed, on bases-query's predicate and on the ranked legs, for the parity reason above. Same day vault_languages left BODYLESS_TOOLS: it gates the note list under max_tier and leaves a row.
